title: Rwanda Eastern Province (Akagera) drought — 2016-2017
brief_outcome_free: Rwanda's drier Eastern Province (Akagera basin) — the country's most drought-prone zone. Rain-fed cropping and livestock; the previous season underperformed. You are the DOC drought analyst.

act1_quiz.prompt: At the mid-2015 lead time, which ENSO state is most relevant to Rwanda's upcoming Season A rainfall forecast?
act1_quiz.hint: A major Pacific event was building through 2015.
options: A strong El Nino, associated with erratic Season A rains over Rwanda and drying over the East African lowlands
A neutral Pacific with no usable forecast signal
A strong La Nina enhancing the long rains
act1_quiz.correct: A strong El Nino, associated with erratic Season A rains over Rwanda and drying over the East African lowlands
act1_quiz.answer_note: The strong 2015-16 El Nino was the dominant large-scale climate signal at this lead time. Over Rwanda it is associated with erratic Season A rains, and the drying anomaly it set up over the East African lowlands extends into the Akagera basin - with a possible swing toward La Nina afterwards adding multi-season uncertainty.
act1_quiz.bn_purpose: Climate-driver context for weighting the seasonal forecast-deficit evidence at long lead.

act1_quiz.prompt: Why is Rwanda's Eastern Province (Akagera basin) the part of the country most exposed to drought?
act1_quiz.hint: Compare it with the wetter western and northern highlands.
options: It lies on the eastern, rain-shadow side of the Congo-Nile divide, so it is the country's driest zone and depends on rain-fed cropping and pasture
It has the country's highest rainfall and steepest terrain
It is irrigated entirely from Lake Kivu
It is fully urbanised and does not depend on agriculture
act1_quiz.correct: It lies on the eastern, rain-shadow side of the Congo-Nile divide, so it is the country's driest zone and depends on rain-fed cropping and pasture
act1_quiz.answer_note: Eastern Rwanda sits in the rain shadow of the Congo-Nile divide, making it climatologically drier than the western and northern highlands. Rain-fed crops and livestock there, including chronically water-scarce areas like Bugesera, have little buffer when seasonal rains under-perform.
act1_quiz.bn_purpose: Exposure context: why a regional rainfall deficit concentrates drought risk in this admin1 rather than nationwide.

decision.checkpoint_prompt: Forecast deficit and CDI agree months ahead of the event window. This is a STRONG, early signal. What DOC level do you set, and what anticipatory action does the ~6-month lead justify?

counterfactual.prompt: What if anticipatory action (water-harvesting/irrigation support and livestock destocking) were triggered at the lead round on the strong forecast signal?
counterfactual.narrative: Slow-onset droughts give long lead. The counterfactual shows the loss-reduction value of acting on a confident seasonal signal rather than waiting for impact confirmation.
